answers: No. Rebase replays commits onto a new base, so each rewritten commit gets a new hash, while the originals remain only in git reflog.
Don't rebase shared history such as main, commits others have built on, or when you need a record of when work was integrated. Use merge there.
Run git rebase --abort to return to the state before the rebase. If it already finished, use git reflog to find the old hash, then git reset --hard to it.
